$comment: Which model a machine STARTS with, and how much of a machine one model may claim.
This file is DATA. No code lives here, so a non-Python host can read it directly.
It names no model above the starter. A fixed ladder from 70 GB down (gpt-oss-120b, Qwen3-32B,
Qwen3-30B-A3B, each with a context) went stale as the models installed here moved on, and a
context written beside a model is a guess the machine can answer: the model past the starter is
the best installed one `poolhouse.serve.suggest.recommend` rates for this machine, and the
context it is served at is `poolhouse.serve.suggest.largest_fit` (the trained window, as much
of it as the memory holds).
Weights are the floor, not the total: KV cache, activations and the runtime's
arena sit on top. These fractions are rough figures and should be described as
such wherever they are shown to a user.
0.7 because a desktop has swap and no low-memory killer, and because the
default GPU wired limit on a large macOS machine is around 0.75 of total.
The 1 GiB overhead floor is sized for a 32k KV cache. Lower usable_fraction
if the machine runs other large processes.
Stricter than desktop: a mobile low-memory killer takes the process rather
than swapping, so the headroom has to be real.
The first install on a machine with little memory: the smallest thing that still
answers, so the first thing a person does finishes while they are still watching
(2.6 GB, about 1.5 s a question, measured: fleet/autostart_models.py DEFAULT_MODEL).
min_ram_gb is the least total memory whose desktop budget above holds weights_gb with
its overhead (the weights plus the 1 GiB floor, at 0.7 of the total: 3.6 GiB / 0.7 =
5.2 GiB); a test checks it. The text-only build, deliberately: a vision-fused variant
of the same language model can be more than twice the size, and some fused builds are
packaged for a different runtime and will not load in llama.cpp.
The floor rung: whatever the target was built with. An embedded image supplies
its own GGUF, so there is no download and no network requirement.
